title: Grandmother wanted Jelly in the trades; his hands and resemblance
summary: Jelly was put to dishwashing, protected his hands, and she looks like him; grandmother wanted her to speak Creole.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: But my grandmother wanted him to be like the rest of the family— carpenters, bricklayers, plasterers, and that kind of work, you know. Butchers, barbers. She had so many sons. She had some in every walk of life, you know what I mean? And she felt like, well, after my mother passed, that my brother should go along with one of my uncles. But just to think they had him dishwashing in a restaurant for three dollars a week, you know. And he—he didn't want his hands to become stiff or broken.

And I—later on in life, I told my grandmother one time about somebody having their legs insured for a million dollars. I said, and that's what brother thought about his hands. He just didn't want his hands to be ruined. He had great big long hands like I have. See what long fingers I have? Yes, yes.
I have big hands. Because you look so much like your brother.

I look just like him. That's right. Surprised to him. And I mean to say this, my grandmother said I had all these mannerisms, and she wanted me to still speak Creole to her. And I mean, I had gotten away from it so long that, I mean, I could remember just certain syllables I would tell her. And then she'd follow the conversation in English. And she said, oh, you have changed so much, child. Your mother would be proud of you today.
